evidence.claim: Code check (exp39 cell 7, linefit_smooth_output_graph): the function does NOT skip fork nodes. A parent with 2 successors gets a one-sided (-2..0) fit. A daughter's backward walk checks only the daughter's predecessor count, so its window CROSSES the fork (parent + grandparent) and pulls it toward the parent line, i.e. toward its sister. But only 0.14% of all nodes (0.27% of a_linefit nodes) have a window that crosses a fork, so defect (ii) as stated is wrong and its fixed form is negligible for edges.
evidence.source: experiments/exp39_sjlee947_tight55_divnetveto notebook cell 7 lines 1299-1370; scratchpad alf.py on tail divnet_rerank_fb435c47e6d4 (656k nodes, 1/8 of videos)

evidence.claim: Symmetric linefit reduces to a fixed FIR filter [.16 .16 .36 .16 .16] (noise gain sum w^2 = 0.232). This matches a CV-model RTS at q/r ~0.5-0.7, or a Whittaker second-difference smoother at lambda = 2 (0.231). At track ends, linefit uses the kernel [-.13 .27 .87] (gain 0.84), against 0.61 for Whittaker lambda 2.
Raw detector coordinates lie on a 1.625-um grid in ALL axes: xy are multiples of 4 voxels, so the grid is isotropic in um and the quantisation sd is 0.47 um per axis.
evidence.source: friend A ckpt tzyx_syn, 44b6_0113de3b and 6bba_fe670320 (99.9% of y/x values are = 0 mod 4)

evidence.claim: Label-free noise estimate from second-difference autocovariances of raw linear chains (12 videos per embryo). r = -lag1/4 in um^2: 44b6 z .55 / y .42 / x .40; 6bba z .80 / y .51 / x .56. The lag-2 estimate is much smaller (.10-.24, about the quantisation variance 0.22), so the model is mis-specified: the lag-1 excess comes from step jumps and ID switches, not white noise. Process variance is also larger in z (6bba q_z 1.24 vs q_y .76). The implied r/q anisotropy is only z/xy ~1.07-1.09. The GT-residual z excess (1.03 vs 0.64 um) is therefore mostly persistent bias or annotation offset, which temporal smoothing cannot remove. Defect (i) is NOT supported as a smoothing-strength argument.
evidence.source: scratchpad noise.py (6 s run); research/discussions_summary.md (Le Quang Canh: annotation bias dz -0.57 um, embryo-dependent)

evidence.claim: Per-video q/r estimated from innovations would imply q/r of 1.3 (lag-1) to ~10 (lag-2). That is LESS smoothing than the empirical B28 optimum (equivalent q/r ~0.5), and B28 showed that weaker smoothing loses (w0.5 -0.0053, win1 -0.0094). So an MMSE-calibrated, label-free per-video noise model would likely under-smooth and lose. The smoothing strength must be calibrated on the metric, not estimated per video.
evidence.source: experiments/RESULTS.md B28 row (12 videos: w0.8/win2 0.9001, off 0.8856, w0.5 0.8948, w1.0 0.8955, win1 0.8907, win3 0.8993); scratchpad kern.py

evidence.claim: a_linefit FN nodes (371 node instances) are boundary cases. Linefit moved them a median of 1.33 um (p90 2.41) out of a match they held at ~6-7 um, so a displacement cap would rescue few. 22% have an unscored (edge_prob 0) edge within +-2 frames, against 13.3% of all nodes. evidence.claim: NEW mechanism found: linefit runs BEFORE the edge filter, stitch and divinsert (kernel tail order linefit -> edgefilter -> swapfix -> stitch -> divinsert). Positions are therefore smoothed along the ~21.5k unscored relink edges (per 64 selection videos) that the edge filter later drops (79% FP among evaluable), and never along the ~15k ILP re-links or the stitch edges that replace them. The edge filter (min_len 0) uses no positions, so re-smoothing from raw coordinates on the FINAL topology changes positions only.

evidence.claim: Literature: u-track and TrackMate use constant-velocity Kalman models for LINKING, with isotropic Euclidean cost and no split handling in TrackMate's Kalman tracker. They do not smooth positions for output. Localisation noise can be estimated label-free from lag covariances (the CVE of Vestergaard 2014). Robust Kalman smoothers (Huber / l1 / Student-t, Aravkin et al.) are the standard fix for outliers and jumps, which our lag-1/lag-2 mismatch shows are present.

implementation_notes: 1) Where: a new final stage resmooth_final_graph, called AFTER divinsert (the last stage), so the node set and edge set are byte-identical to the control and the node multiplier is exactly 1.000. It restores RAW positions and re-smooths on the final topology. Kernel side: in linefit_smooth_output_graph, stash original_pos in a module-level dict RAW_POS (not in node dicts, to keep the GEFF attributes unchanged). Replay side: take raw coords from ckpt tzyx_syn by node_id (verified exact; tail adds no nodes). Ship as tools/build_probe_kernel.py --patch resmooth with RESMOOTH_ENABLE=0 meaning an exact no-op; replay keys rs.*, post-tail like st.*/sw.*. 2) Segments: consecutive t->t+1 edges where the source has 1 successor and the target has 1 predecessor. A fork ends the parent segment at the parent, and each daughter starts a new segment (one-sided); this fixes the fork-crossing daughter window. Option rs.break_unscored: also cut a segment at an edge with edge_prob None/0 (unscored relink), for smoothing only, without touching topology. Keep synthetic gap nodes; they are interpolations and smooth harmlessly. 3) Smoother: use a Whittaker / second-difference penalised least squares per segment and per axis rather than a hand-coded RTS. Minimise sum w_t (x_t - y_t)^2 + lambda * sum (x_{t+1} - 2x_t + x_{t-1})^2 with scipy.linalg.solve_banded (pentadiagonal; closed form, fast, no velocity init issue). It is the MAP estimate of the integrated-random-walk (CV) model, i.e. an RTS with lambda = r/q. Blend new = (1 - a) * y + a * fit with a = 1 by default. lambda = 2 reproduces the linefit interior noise gain; segments of length < 3 stay raw (as linefit does). Robust option: IRLS Huber weights w_t = min(1, c / |resid_t|) with c = 1.5 um, 3 iterations; an outlier node is then not allowed to drag its neighbours. Per-axis option: lambda_z = k * lambda_xy (positions in um). 4) Do NOT set lambda from per-video innovation statistics. Measured label-free q/r implies less smoothing than the metric optimum, and the lag-1/lag-2 mismatch shows jump contamination. If a per-video factor is wanted at all, use only a clipped relative factor (video r/q over the median r/q, clipped to [0.7, 1.4]) as a late variant. 5) Pitfalls: (a) scale positions to um before smoothing or the z/xy lambda is inconsistent; per-axis polyfit in voxels is scale-invariant, but a z/xy ratio is not. (b) divinsert reads positions: placing resmooth before divinsert changes insertions, so keep it after. (c) The x138 float-coordinate port removes most of the 0.47-um quantisation noise, so the optimal lambda will DROP; re-run the lambda row after the port (the old w0.8 linefit may then over-smooth). (d) The pre-relink variant changes topology, needs a new tail base key (pre-tail) and inherits the relink's weak LB transfer. Excluded from round 1. (e) Divisions: only ~66 predicted division events locally (TP 23 / FP 43), so the division readout is quantised noise; do not select on it.
refined_change: Replace the hypothesis (a per-axis RTS with per-video noise estimates, run pre-relink) with a FINAL-TOPOLOGY RE-SMOOTH: after divinsert, restore the raw detector positions and re-smooth each fork-split linear segment of the final graph. This undoes linefit having run before the edge filter, stitch and divinsert, and so having smoothed along the ~21.5k/64-video unscored relink edges that are later dropped (79% FP). Step 1 (zero new knobs): the same linefit (w0.8, win2) recomputed on the final topology, plus a fork split. Step 2: a Whittaker/RTS-equivalent smoother (lambda around 2 = the linefit-equivalent gain) with optional cuts at unscored edges, Huber IRLS and a z/xy lambda ratio. Positions change, topology does not: N_pred and edges are identical to the control. Per-video label-free noise estimation and the pre-relink variant are dropped (not supported by the measurements).
refined_lab_test: Kaggle-CPU replay lab, post-tail stage (no new base key; raw coords from ckpt by node_id; assert node/edge sets identical to control and multiplier == 1.000000). Control = the current best local stack (lp_ef_a3_rl_pr, + stitch if adopted). SELECTION grid (64 6bba videos, 11 configs): rs0 = linefit w0.8/win2 on the final topology, no fork split; rs1 = rs0 + fork split; rs2 = rs1 + cut at unscored (edge_prob None/0) edges; wh_l1 / wh_l2 / wh_l3 = Whittaker lambda 1/2/3 isotropic, fork split + unscored cut; wh_l2_z15, wh_l2_z2 = lambda_z = 1.5x / 2x lambda_xy; wh_l2_hub = wh_l2 + Huber IRLS c = 1.5 um, 3 iterations; cap2 = rs1 with a 2.0-um displacement cap (the L6 report's GT-free idea); wh_l2_nocut = the fork split without the unscored cut, to isolate the cut. Pick the best, then run ONE CONFIRMATION (135 videos): gate >= +0.002, each embryo >= +0.001, gains on >= 55% of changed videos per embryo, 90% bootstrap CI lower bound > 0. Report per embryo: dJ_edge (the multiplier must be exactly 1), edge TP/FP/FN deltas, the number of GT matches that change, the median distance to matched GT (all nodes and division nodes), and division TP/FP (informational only, quantised). Cheap pre-check before any Kaggle run (local, nice, < 1 min per video): the fraction of final-graph nodes whose rs0 position differs from the shipped position by > 0.5 um; if < 1%, expect no signal. If the x138 float-coordinate port ships, re-run wh_l1/wh_l2/rs1 on the float coords. No GPU needed.
expected_gain: +0.0005 to +0.002 local and public (a guess). The largest plausible part is rs0/rs2: removing smoothing along dropped FP relink edges, which cause about half of all > 2 um linefit moves. Kernel shape, per-axis lambda and the fork split are each expected at <= +0.0005, because the anisotropy of r/q is only ~1.08 and forks touch 0.14% of nodes. Ceiling about +0.0025 (the a_linefit 353 FN x 7.1e-6), and not all of them are reachable, since their median move is only 1.3 um at the matching boundary. It is not a route to 0.97 on its own. Transfer risk is low: a position-only change with no network outputs and an unchanged node count.
